intelligence.essence: Project Intelligence is the one record the whole system works from: every piece of work is an item with an honest state, every act of work ends as a visible state change with proof or it counts as waste, and "done" is a database write the system refuses without evidence from a different seat. Its loop is PRODUCE → PROVE → PUBLISH → SEE, its face is a derivation from the record (never a report typed beside it), and its build order runs claim → build → scorecard → verify → land, stopping only when the whole scope is done and proven. Underneath sits the definition that makes it intelligence rather than bookkeeping: to "get it" is for understanding to finish its journey into changed behavior — and PI is the project's model of itself.
intelligence.human_view: Before this, the project kept its truth in a dozen places that disagreed — items "done" with no proof, counts that didn't match, blockers with nowhere to live. Project Intelligence is the one book: write the state honestly, prove it with someone else's eyes, and let every screen be a window into that same book instead of a new story.
intelligence.child_view: Imagine one big notebook for the whole team. Every job is written in it, and you may only write "finished" if a friend checks your work and signs beside you. If you're stuck, you write exactly what's stuck and who can unstick it. Everyone reads the same notebook, so nobody has a different story.
intelligence.grandma_view: It's the household ledger done right: every entry accounted for, nothing marked paid that wasn't, and a second pair of eyes on the important lines. The book doesn't just remember — it refuses a dishonest entry, the way a good bookkeeper refuses a receipt-less expense.
intelligence.ai_view: Work the loop: PRODUCE → PROVE → PUBLISH → SEE, and let nothing you do end without a state change and proof. Claim before you build — the claim is the lock. Never mark done_proven without an evidence URL and a prover who isn't you; never park a blocker without {what, owner, since, clearing_action}; never raise a needs_shawn without its packet in the same transaction. Treat the six waste classes as alarms pointed at yourself: if your loop ran twenty times with zero transitions, you are W1 today. And check your understanding by the four-part test, not by the feeling of knowing.
intelligence.what_it_means: A collective can only be as intelligent as its shared model of itself. PI is that model made operational: a record that enforces honesty at write time, derives every face from one truth, and measures the one ratio that separates production from motion. The "get it" doctrine is its soul: the record exists so that behavior changes — a project that understands itself regulates itself.
whats_inside: One record, one derivation, one face: numbers computed from the record at read time, never typed beside it.
States are honest or the write is refused: proof from a different seat is a database constraint, not a custom.
Waste is a measured set of six named classes, each with a detector — not a feeling about the week.
The ratio is the headline: production over activity, published daily, null rather than faked.
A record nobody's behavior changes because of is storage, not intelligence.
